name: 精灵系统
description: The pet domain. Owns the legacy `pets` table, serves the 17 pet routes the frontend already calls (migrated out of api/modules/pet in P4.3b.6), publishes `pet.public`, enforces pet.adopt / pet.interact on its own alias routes, and reaches students, the point ledger and the class feature flags through `classroom.public`.

data._adopted_note: `pets` is the domain's real table, carrying its legacy name until P7 renames it to `p_pet_pets`. It replaced the P3 reference table of nearly that name, which this plugin's own `0002_retire_reference_tables` migration drops: the two are different tables, and only `pets` ever held live data (3 rows in the developer database; `p_pet_pets` was empty).
data._reads_note: Both are declared READS because a read is all this domain needs, and neither has an owner to ask yet. `praises` (teacher praise shown on the pet dashboard) belongs to no plugin - it is classroom-adjacent data that P7 should either move into classroom or expose through a port. `parent_activity` is owned by plugins/parent-buff, which writes it from its own route; the pet domain reads `last_active_date` to answer `has_parent_buff`, and that column exists in the kernel composition only because of api/schema/legacyCompatColumns.ts. The correct fix for both is a port (`parent-buff.public.hasTodayBuff`, `classroom.public.listPraises`) once those plugins publish one; until then an undeclared read would be refused by ctx.db, so this is honest rather than silent.
data._known_debt: The 17 legacy READ routes are unauthenticated, exactly as they were in api/modules/pet: HANDOFF §10 item 3 records that the tree-wide authorization round is still pending and docs/security/route-authorization-matrix.md tracks it per endpoint; plugins/pet is one of its batches. The four WRITE routes are no longer part of that debt: `/adoptions` and `/actions` (the twins `src/features/pet/api/petApi.ts` actually calls) now run the same requireActor + ctx.permissions.require gate as this plugin's own `/adopt` and `/action` aliases, so pet.adopt / pet.interact can no longer be bypassed by picking the unguarded twin - before that they gated nothing reachable. Also: `interact` deducts points through the classroom port and then updates `pets`; the two writes cannot share a transaction across the plugin boundary (see the service header).
